events.headline: Russia, Ukraine and the US resume three-way peace talks in Abu Dhabi
events.summary: Delegations from Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened a two-day round of US-mediated negotiations in the UAE capital, the first three-way meeting since February.

facts.text: The talks are scheduled for 10–11 November and are the first trilateral session since a round in Geneva in February.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead the US side; Rustem Umerov heads Ukraine's delegation and Vladimir Medinsky Russia's.
What, if anything, has been agreed on territory or security guarantees has not been made public.

updates.text: First day ended after roughly four hours; a second session was set for Wednesday.
Zelensky said the first day dealt largely with humanitarian questions, including prisoner exchanges and the return of civilians and children.

facts.text: A large prisoner exchange, described as 1,000 for 1,000 or more, was agreed in principle according to unnamed sources; details were still to be worked out.
facts.by: Interfax-Ukraine sources; a senior Ukrainian official speaking anonymously to AP

updates.text: Umerov said the second day had begun, starting with a three-way session followed by a separate meeting with European representatives.

movement.label: Delegations convene in Abu Dhabi
movement.note: Schematic. Lines join each delegation's capital to the venue to show who met where. They are not flight paths, and departure points and times were not reported.

events.headline: Drone attack hits Kirishi oil refinery in Russia's Leningrad Oblast
events.summary: A drone attack struck the Kinef refinery at Kirishi, one of Russia's largest, during the night of 8–9 November. The regional governor acknowledged the attack; Ukraine is reported to have carried it out.

facts.text: Leningrad Oblast governor Aleksandr Drozdenko confirmed a drone attack on the refinery.
Ukrainian monitoring channels reported large explosions at the plant, which lies roughly 800 km north of Ukraine.
facts.by: Exilenova+ and Supernova+ channels, via Kyiv Independent

facts.text: The launch area, the route flown and the extent of damage have not been established. No route is drawn for that reason.

sources.title: Ukraine strikes Russia's second-largest oil refinery in overnight drone attack, Russian governor says

events.headline: Bridge over the Mius River and power stations reported hit in Rostov Oblast
events.place: Mius River crossing on the R-280 highway, Rostov Oblast, Russia
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck targets in Russia's Rostov Oblast on the morning of 8 November, according to the regional governor, including a bridge on a road linking the region with Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

facts.text: Drone debris damaged the bridge carrying the R-280 highway over the Mius River, and power stations were also hit.
facts.by: Rostov Oblast governor, via Kyiv Independent

facts.text: A monitoring channel published footage it said showed the strike and attributed it to an FP-2 drone. The footage has not been independently confirmed in the reporting used here.
The exact crossing point is not specified in the reporting, so the location is drawn as an approximate area.

sources.title: Ukrainian drones hit key bridge, power stations in Russia's Rostov Oblast, governor says

events.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya
events.summary: The UN climate conference began on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast with nearly 200 countries represented. The hosts are framing it as a summit about carrying out existing pledges rather than setting new targets.

facts.text: The conference runs from 9 to 20 November. Türkiye's environment minister Murat Kurum presides, while Australia's Chris Bowen steers the negotiations under a shared arrangement agreed at COP30.
The United States is not taking part.
Attendance estimates differ: UN News expected more than 90,000 people; other outlets cite more than 100,000.

updates.text: A two-day leaders' segment was scheduled for 11–12 November.

sources.title: COP31 opens in Antalya: Can climate promises finally deliver results?

events.headline: Gunman kills six in Kraków's Main Market Square
events.summary: A man drove into Kraków's central square around midday on Saturday and fired from his car at people nearby. Police shot and arrested him within minutes.

facts.text: First reports in Polish media put the death toll at five or more.

updates.text: Toll established at six dead, four women and two men, with about 15 wounded; two police officers were also hurt.
updates.by: Kraków police, via CNN and CBS News

replaceFacts.text: Six people were killed and around 15 wounded. Two police officers who stopped the attacker were injured.
replaceFacts.by: Kraków police, via CNN and CBS News

updates.text: Three relatives of the attacker were found dead at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. The interior minister said he held radical nationalist views.

facts.text: The bodies of the attacker's mother, father and sister were found at his home.

updates.text: The attacker, 24, died in hospital at 04:30 local time. Officials stepped back from earlier statements about motive.
updates.by: Polish police, via NBC News and CNBC

facts.text: Motive. The interior minister first pointed to far-right ideology; on Monday officials declined to name a motive after opposition politicians challenged the basis for the claim.

updates.text: The justice minister said the attacker had visited websites about Anders Behring Breivik and described a strong indication of right-wing extremism. The investigation continues.

events.headline: Two passenger trains collide at Al-Ayyat, south of Cairo
events.summary: A train running from Giza to Fayoum struck the rear of a stationary Cairo–Aswan service between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations, derailing several carriages.

Early Health Ministry figures: at least four dead and 88 injured.

events.headline: South Africa's local elections: ANC falls to about 31 per cent
events.place: National Results Operation Centre, Midrand, South Africa
events.summary: South Africans voted for municipal councils on 4 November, with special votes on the two preceding days. 10,526 seats in 213 councils were contested.

facts.text: Voting took place on 4 November, with special votes on 2–3 November.
Results were not yet declared.

updates.text: With about half of voting districts counted, provisional figures put the ANC near 32 per cent. The IEC stressed that nothing was final until declared.

replaceFacts.text: Voting took place on 4 November, with special votes on 2–3 November.
Provisional count at the halfway mark: ANC about 31.8 per cent.

updates.text: The IEC declared the elections free and fair and announced final results.

replaceFacts.text: Final result: ANC 30.76 per cent, down from 45.59 per cent in 2021; it remains the largest party.
Turnout was 52 per cent, about 14.9 million voters, up 6.1 points on 2021.
Only 74 of 213 councils have an outright majority; 139 will need coalitions.
One voting centre faces a re-vote after ballots were destroyed.

events.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: Iran's IRGC said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents on Wednesday evening after using routes through the strait that Iran does not authorise. The account comes from one party to the conflict.

facts.text: One tanker struck a mine south of the strait; a second caught fire in the eastern part, as did a tug that came to help.
The IRGC did not name the vessels, their flags or owners, or give casualties or damage.

updates.text: Iran's army said three more tankers had struck mines east of the strait, bringing the Iranian count to five tankers and a tug.

The IRGC said three further tankers were ablaze. Separately, the UK maritime agency UKMTO reported a tanker on fire off Khasab, Oman, with its crew evacuated, and another hit by an unidentified projectile.

facts.text: UKMTO independently reported at least one tanker fire in the strait on 7 November.
The total number of ships hit. UKMTO has said many ships no longer report attacks, so counts cannot be reconciled.

events.headline: Earthquake in western Shizuoka injures at least 24
events.summary: An earthquake struck central Japan at 01:04 local time on 8 November, disrupting rail services. The strongest shaking was recorded at Chita in Aichi Prefecture.

facts.text: No deaths and no tsunami warning were reported; the Hamaoka nuclear plant showed no abnormalities.
At least 24 people were injured; the figure is provisional.
Magnitude. Japan's Meteorological Agency gave a preliminary 5.7; the US Geological Survey measured 5.5.

events.headline: Flooding forces evacuations across the US Southwest
events.place: Four Corners region: Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico
events.summary: Heavy rain on 1 November fell on already saturated ground, closing roads and prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Arizona, Colorado and New Mexico.

facts.text: Rising water in Oak Creek at Sedona, Arizona, trapped residents, some of whom were lifted from rooftops by helicopter.
The San Juan River at Pagosa Springs, Colorado, was forecast to crest at 21.9 feet.

updates.text: Waters began to recede, leaving mud and damaged homes; clean-up started in some communities.

events.headline: Bolivian urban teachers begin 48-hour strike
events.summary: Teachers in Bolivia's cities walked out for two days against government plans to hand responsibility for education to regional authorities. Some are also on hunger strike.

facts.text: Teachers argue decentralisation would deepen inequality and comes without funding guarantees.
The strike is nationwide in urban areas; the marker sits on La Paz for convenience and the start date (8 or 9 November) is not pinned down in the reporting used here.

sources.title: World in brief: November 10, 2026

events.headline: Floods affect thousands in North Sumatra
events.place: Deli Serdang and Serdang Bedagai, North Sumatra, Indonesia
events.summary: Flooding on 5 and 7 November affected about 9,600 people in two North Sumatra regencies, according to Indonesia's disaster agency.

facts.text: About 9,600 people in 2,400 families were affected.

updates.text: Indonesia's weather agency placed North Sumatra on its highest alert for very heavy to extreme rain from 9 to 12 November. Flooding also reached Gayo Lues in Aceh on 8 November.
updates.by: BMKG and BNPB, via the AHA Centre
